subject: Re: Data residency & deployment options — EU/APAC availability
messages:
From: Anders Holm <anders.holm@fintech-eu.com>

Date: Sat, 09 May 2026 13:12:00 +0200
Subject: Thanks — quick follow-up on residency requirements

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the intro/demo today — super helpful overview. A couple of clarifications from our side so we can scope internally: 

- Data residency: our compliance team requires that all production customer data remain within the EU (no cross-border replication or routing to non-EU regions).
- Failover: we need an understanding of cross-region failover behavior. If you offer EU-hosted endpoints, will any traffic ever route through a non-EU region (for failover or capacity)?
- Deployment mode: our security lead prefers not to do on-prem if we can meet residency + isolation requirements in a managed offering. We're open to Dedicated capacity (reserved) if it guarantees isolation and logs.
- Compliance artifacts: please share SOC2 / encryption and KMS options, and whether you support customer-managed keys.

Can you confirm what is possible with Redwood Hosted API in the EU vs Dedicated vs Private VPC? Also if there are any known limitations for strict residency (e.g., CDN edges, logging, backups)?

I'll loop in our security team after we get those details — they may have a short questionnaire.

Best,
Anders
Head of Infrastructure
Fintech EU

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 08:02:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Thanks — quick follow-up on residency requirements

Hi Anders — great speaking with you yesterday. Recap below and proposed next steps so your security/compliance team has what they need.

Recap / answers to your points:
- Hosted API (EU): We operate a Hosted API region in eu-west-1 and can enable EU-only data residency for your account. When residency is enabled we restrict storage and primary processing to the region; control-plane metadata (account configs) remains in our control plane but is logically separated.
- Cross-region failover: By default we have multi-region failover capabilities for availability, but for customers that require strict residency we can disable cross-region automatic failover and configure region-locked routing. In that mode traffic and storage remain in EU; we do not route request payloads through non-EU regions.
- Dedicated capacity: Dedicated (reserved) capacity provisioned in the EU gives you isolated GPU pools and predictable throughput. Logs, KV caches, and model artifacts can be configured to stay in-region. This is a common option for customers who want managed service but need stronger tenancy boundaries.
- Private / VPC: Private offers VPC peering and an on-prem install option. On-prem gives you full physical control; VPC mode provides private networking while the control plane can remain managed. Both support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and audit log exports.
- Compliance artifacts: attaching our latest SOC 2 Type II and a deployment requirements template. We support customer-managed KMS for Dedicated and Private; Hosted can use customer-managed keys via KMS in many enterprise contracts (we'll include this in the SOC annex).

Known limitations & notes:
- CDN edges: small amounts of metadata (e.g., public model list) may be globally cached; actual customer payloads and model inference IO remain in-region when residency is enabled.
- Backups / long term storage: we can restrict backups to region, but for disaster recovery customers sometimes choose a cold DR site; we can document and restrict accordingly.

Next steps:
1) I attached a short deployment requirements matrix (fintech-deployment-requirements-template.xlsx) — if you can have your security team fill the highlighted sections we can map to Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private recommendations.
2) Jordan (cc) is our solutions lead and can run a technical deep-dive with your infra/security team next week. Please propose 2x 45-min slots.
3) Rishi (cc) will prepare a draft pricing comparison (Hosted w/ EU residency vs Dedicated EU reserve vs Private VPC) once we have expected throughput and retention needs.

If you prefer a single managed option that meets strict residency + CMK + audit logs, Dedicated in the EU is often the right balance. But many customers choose Hosted with residency enabled for faster time-to-value.

Thanks — attaching SOC2 and the matrix.

Best,
